title: Blue-hour sky as a two-stop gradient, never a starfield
note: A tagged gradient sky dome and nothing tagged star: a sky sprinkled with stars to the zenith lost a whole facet.
intent: A sky sprinkled with stars to the zenith was the standing rejection of a whole 20-iteration facet, and the agent otherwise oscillates between hard starfield, flat uniform blue and gradient because every iteration overcorrects. Pin the sky at init to a two-stop vertical gradient with explicit hex values — zenith #0d1b2e to horizon #2f5d8c for blue-hour — with a haze band hugging the horizon, matched by the FogExp2 colour so the far plane dissolves, and do not touch it between iterations unless a check flags it flat or too dark. No starfield: if the brief allows stars at all, cap their elevation well below the zenith.

check.note: A tagged gradient sky dome exists and nothing tagged star/starfield does; a sky sprinkled with stars to the zenith lost a whole 20-iteration facet.

port: Add makeSky() to the lighting/atmosphere module, tag the dome "sky", set the two hex stops as named constants in the brief and never edit them in later iterations; any star sprites must be tagged "star" so the check can see them. Re-verify the distinct-camera check after changing sky or fog, since a fully fogged scene makes every camera render the same frame.

evidence.note: sky background a vertical gradient #0d1b2e → #2f5d8c, never a starfield; stars to the zenith lost a 20-iteration facet
sky/ambient oscillation guard: pin a two-stop gradient with explicit hex at init and do not touch it between iterations
"blue-hour" alone produces starfield-black or flat blue; brief must give top and bottom hex
blue-hour checklist (a): deep top colour to warmer horizon, not a flat dark or starfield
